achievements.title: IEEEBIG 2026 National Finalist
achievements.description: Co-developed ECOS, an end-of-life EV battery management framework. Built risk-assessment heatmap and contributed to financial model.
fullDescription: Team Elpatron reached the national finals of the 2026 IEEEBIG case competition with ECOS (EcoBat Circular Ownership System), a proposed framework for managing end-of-life EV batteries in Indonesia. The system combines a Battery-as-a-Service deposit scheme, a collection network leveraging existing SPKLU charging infrastructure, and a battery grading facility for second-life applications.

My primary contribution was the risk assessment module. I identified twelve operational and financial risk factors across the supply chain, scored each on probability and impact axes, and built a heatmap visualization in Python (matplotlib) that became the team's anchor slide.

I also contributed to financial-viability reverse engineering: revenue projections of Rp 9.2 trillion, net margin of 88%, BaaS customer base ranging 28K to 443K over five years. The competition required bilingual deliverables (English report, Indonesian pitch) and consulting-style presentation work modeled on BCG and McKinsey deck conventions.
highlights: Financial model: Rp 9.2T revenue, 88% net margin

achievements.title: HSSE Data Analyst Intern
achievements.description: Bias-corrected satellite rainfall against gauge data. Built siren-threshold recommendations from lag-correlation analysis at extensometer stations.
fullDescription: Six-week internship at ANTAM's Pongkor gold mine working with the Health, Safety, Security & Environment department. The core problem: the mine's slope-monitoring early-warning system relied on rainfall thresholds that did not account for satellite-product bias or cumulative rainfall history.

Bias correction. Pulled GPM IMERG and CHIRPS satellite rainfall, applied Linear Scaling and Quantile Mapping in Python against ground rain-gauge records, benchmarked which combination performed best at the site scale.

Lag analysis. Ran cross-correlation between corrected rainfall and displacement readings from two extensometer stations. Identified statistically significant lag windows that informed threshold redesign.

Siren threshold review. Tested the existing operational threshold against one year of field data. Found cases where it missed antecedent-rainfall and multi-day cumulative patterns, and recommended a revised threshold logic.

Spatial context. Used DEMNAS in QGIS to produce elevation and slope-class maps of the concession area for landslide-susceptibility context. Presented four operational recommendations directly to HSSE leadership.
highlights: Two bias-correction methods benchmarked on satellite rainfall
Cross-correlation analysis on two extensometer stations
Four formal recommendations to HSSE leadership

achievements.title: Climate Change Analysis Intern
achievements.description: Statistical downscaling of CMIP6 climate model outputs. Validated against CHIRPS for mining-sector risk assessment.
fullDescription: Four-week internship at BMKG's Climate Change Information Centre. Focus: making global climate model outputs usable at site scale for mining-industry risk assessment.

Statistical downscaling. Applied Linear Scaling bias correction to CMIP6 global climate model outputs in Python, generating higher-resolution projection datasets aligned to Indonesian station locations.
Validation. Compared downscaled outputs against CHIRPS satellite rainfall records to quantify residual bias and assess how well the method preserved real-world rainfall statistics.

Tooling. Built reusable Python workflows in xarray and netCDF4 to process multi-gigabyte climate datasets. Presented methodology and findings to the Climate Change Information Centre team at the end of the placement.

achievements.title: Head of RnD, Atmosphaira ITB
achievements.description: Led a 10-person team building IoT-based water-level and rainfall recorders, deployed as early-warning tools in a partner village.
fullDescription: Led the Research and Development division of Atmosphaira, the ITB Meteorology Student Association, for a full term. The division of 10 people split across hardware, firmware, and modeling tracks.

Hardware program. Took an IoT-based Automatic Water Level Recorder (AWLR) and Automatic Rainfall Recorder (ARR) from prototype to field deployment in a partner village, where they now function as community early-warning tools.
Modeling. Ran WRF-Hydro hydrometeorological simulations in parallel with the hardware work to produce predictive rainfall and discharge maps that informed where the recorders should be placed.

Operations. Managed task delegation, weekly sprint reviews, and stakeholder coordination with faculty supervisors and external partners. Closed the term with a formal post-mortem document to transfer lessons to the next division head.
highlights: AWLR + ARR shipped to a partner village
Formal handover post-mortem to next term
